title: [D3 Enrichment] Enrichment status propagation acceptance tests
summary: tests/test_acceptance_enrichment.py is the named gate D4 is blocked on: ten tests that build each of the six enrichment states out of real ingest and the real ThreatFox loader and then read helena_analytical_enriched_context. Four of them are properties over the whole space rather than one state -- every status distinguishable in one store across four windows, no incomplete query carrying a classification of any kind, a stale negative never mistakable for a fresh one, and a coverage assertion against ENRICHMENT_STATUSES so the gate cannot quietly stop covering a status. `acceptance` is a registered pytest marker and `make acceptance` runs the gate alone; the tests are part of `make test` either way.
assumption_validated: THE SIXTH STATE HAS NO NAME, AND MUST NOT GET ONE. The task asks for an `in-flight load` fixture, and there is no `in_flight` outcome in the ledger -- outcomes are `loaded`, `unchanged`, `failed` -- because a load in flight has not finished having an outcome. What makes it safe is an ORDERING, not a status: `load_threatfox` writes its claims, FLUSHes, and only then writes the ledger row, so the ledger row is the commit point and a snapshot nothing has committed has no validity interval to be joined through. Measured rather than argued: with the claims of a real completed load still in `helena_reference_threatfox` and only its ledger row removed, the entity that was a hit becomes status `missing` with `classification` NULL and `evidence_id` NULL -- neither a hit nor a clean lookup. Adding an `in_flight` status would have been inventing a fifth value for a state the design already handles by construction, and `concept/instruction.md` §2 forbids a value that stands for something another value already says.
makes_buildable: D4 triage can be built against a row it is allowed to trust. The gate proves the five facts a rendering has to keep apart -- ok / stale / failed / missing / no_match -- are each reachable and each distinct in the view D4 reads, so the rendering task can treat `status` and `classification` as two independent columns without re-deriving why. It also gives D4 a regression gate that fails loudly rather than a convention: `make acceptance` is the command, and test_the_gate_covers_every_status_the_model_defines fails if a status is ever added without a fixture.

verification.detail: 775 passed, 0 skipped (765 before, 10 new), against a throwaway in-memory ./bin/risingwave single_node. `make acceptance` alone is 10 passed, 765 deselected in ~50 s. MUTATION-CHECKED TWICE, each restored byte-identically (md5 verified) and re-run green. (1) Changing 0015's classification CASE from `WHEN v.snapshot_version IS NOT NULL THEN 'no_match'` to `ELSE 'no_match'` -- so an incomplete query yields a taxonomy object -- fails exactly three: the failed-load test, the missing-window test, and test_no_query_that_did_not_complete_carries_a_classification, which reports `status 'missing' carried classification 'no_match'`. (2) Changing the status CASE's `ELSE 'stale'` to `ELSE 'ok'` fails exactly four: the stale test, the four-window distinguishability test, test_a_stale_negative_is_never_mistakable_for_a_fresh_one, and the coverage test. Both mutations are ones a plausible refactor could make, and both are caught by the property tests rather than only by the single-state ones.
verification.first_run_note: All ten passed on the first run, which is why both mutations were done before the report was written. A gate that has never been seen to fail is a gate nobody has tested.

invariant_conflicts.step: Assert no path exists by which a stale or failed feed can produce `no_match`
invariant_conflicts.conflict: Half of this contradicts `concept/02-concepts-and-taxonomy.md`, which outranks prd.json in the authority order (prds/CONTEXT.md §1). `no_match` is defined there as 'the source COMPLETED its query and returned no record'. A stale snapshot did complete its query -- it completed it a while ago -- so a stale snapshot holding no claim about an entity is a genuine negative with a date on it, and the view already says both (`status = 'stale'` beside `classification = 'no_match'`). Forbidding that pair would leave two options and both are worse: drop the row, which is the absent-row failure mode this whole suite exists to prevent, or relabel a real negative as something else, which loses the fact that the source answered at all.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: The half concept/02 does require is asserted, and asserted over the whole space rather than one example: a query that did not complete -- `failed`, `missing`, or in flight -- carries no classification of any kind, not `no_match` and not `unknown`. test_no_query_that_did_not_complete_carries_a_classification walks every row of a four-window store and also asserts the converse, so it cannot pass by producing no classifications at all. The half it does not require is replaced by what the reader actually needs, which is to tell an aged negative from a current one: test_a_stale_negative_is_never_mistakable_for_a_fresh_one builds two windows whose ONLY difference is snapshot age, and asserts same classification, different status. The disagreement and its reasoning are in the module docstring, not only here, because the next person to read the suite will be looking for the assertion the task named.

deferred: A fixture for `sslbl-ja3`. It is registered in helena.enrichment.SOURCES and has no loader, so it can never appear in the view -- the source list is read off the snapshot ledger, which is every source that has ever been ASKED. tests/test_enriched.py already asserts that consequence and `feed_status` is what reports `missing` for such a source. Duplicating it here would be a second answer to a question already answered.

An in-flight fixture for a source's FIRST ever load. With no ledger row at all the source is not in the view's CROSS JOIN, so the entity produces no row for it rather than a `missing` row -- the same behaviour as a source never asked. The suite tests the subsequent-load case instead, which is the one where a part-written snapshot could actually be mistaken for a landed one.

Asserting the loader's write order directly. The suite proves the property the order exists for -- an uncommitted snapshot is unreadable -- by reproducing the intermediate state, not by asserting that the INSERTs precede the ledger write. A test over statement order would be a test about the implementation rather than about what a reader can see.
Wiring the gate into CI. There is no CI here yet; `make acceptance` is the command and the Makefile comment says what it is for.
lessons: THE LEDGER ROW IS THE COMMIT POINT for a feed snapshot. Claims can be fully written into helena_reference_threatfox and remain completely invisible to the enriched context, because the join goes through helena_reference_feed_snapshot_validity and there is no interval until the ledger row lands. This is what makes a part-written load safe, and it is worth knowing before adding a second feed: a loader that wrote its ledger row FIRST would expose a half-written snapshot as a complete one.

STATUS IS A PROPERTY OF (WINDOW, LOAD HISTORY), NEVER OF AN ENTITY. Every entity in the same window sees the same status from the same source; only `classification` varies per entity. So a test that wants two statuses needs two windows, and the four-window construction in test_the_states_are_distinguishable_in_one_store is the shape any later status test should copy: place the attempts, then place the windows among them.

The freshness comparison and the join predicate pull in opposite directions and both have to be satisfied. `e.window_start >= v.valid_from` needs the snapshot loaded at or before the window; `v.valid_from > now() - refresh_interval` needs it loaded recently. Loading AT the window's own start satisfies both, and ThreatFox's 3600 s refresh against a 300 s window leaves an order-of-magnitude margin, so the fresh/stale fixtures are not timing-sensitive. A source with a refresh interval near the window size would make them so.

A source with no refresh interval can never be stale -- the view's first CASE branch returns `ok` when refresh_interval_seconds IS NULL. That is task 22's decision (static since 2021 is not late, it is finished) reaching the analytical layer, and it means a coverage test over statuses must use a scheduled source.

MEASURED: a worktree built by prds/CONTEXT.md §4's link recipe runs the suite with TWO SKIPS, not zero -- `data/demo` is gitignored and is not in the recipe's list. Added to the recipe in this task. Everything else in the list was correct, and with data/demo linked the worktree suite matches the main tree's exactly.

The acceptance marker is registered in pyproject.toml and `--strict-markers` is on, so a test marked `acceptance` in a file nobody registered would error rather than silently not run. That is what makes `make acceptance` a gate rather than a naming convention.
failed_approaches: Constructing the in-flight state by calling the loader's private `_insert_threatfox_row` to write claims without a ledger row. Rejected before it was written: it reaches into a private helper to reproduce a state the public path already produces, and a test coupled to a private function stops testing the public one. Running the real loader and then deleting only its ledger row reaches the identical state -- claims written by the real code, commit point absent -- through the public API.

Deleting the ONLY ledger row to make the in-flight state. That empties helena_reference_feed_snapshot, and the view's source list is `SELECT DISTINCT source_id` from exactly that table, so the source disappears from the CROSS JOIN and the entity produces no rows at all rather than unreadable ones. The test therefore asserts the hit FIRST, then removes the ledger row, so the assertion is about a row that changed rather than a row that vanished.
next_session_should_know: D4 is gated on `make acceptance` and the gate is real -- it was seen to fail under two separate mutations before this report was written, and the mutations are named in `verification` so you can repeat them. Four things to carry into the rendering task. (1) `status` and `classification` are INDEPENDENT columns and the rendering must keep them so: `no_match` is a classification on a row whose query succeeded, and there are exactly four statuses. A rendering that folds them into one field is the failure this whole stage exists to prevent, and test_no_query_that_did_not_complete_carries_a_classification is what will catch it if the view is what changed. (2) A stale `no_match` is legitimate and will appear in real data -- see invariant_conflicts. What a rendering owes the agent is the age, not the suppression: the row carries `snapshot_loaded_at` and `snapshot_version` for exactly that. (3) The enriched context is MOSTLY NEGATIVE SPACE by construction, so a bounded rendering will be truncating mostly-no_match rows; truncation that drops the negatives and keeps the hits would hand triage a store that looks like nothing but threats, which is the same misreading from the other side. (4) If you add a status, test_the_gate_covers_every_status_the_model_defines fails until the gate grows a fixture for it. That is deliberate -- it is the mechanism that keeps this suite honest as the vocabulary changes.
